DermaTwin — Algorithm & Formula Reference

THEIA-Core Engine v4.2 · Reproducibility Specification · 2026-09-06

1. Image Preprocessing Pipeline

1.1 Inverse LUT Conversion

Input: Dermascan pseudo-color RGB image (101-entry palette, echo 0–100).

  1. Build 101-entry forward LUT: LUT[echo] → {R, G, B} from Dermascan hardware palette. Color order: Black → Green → Blue → Purple → Red → Orange → Yellow (echo 0 → 100).
  2. Build inverse cache: 64×64×64 quantized RGB lookup. For each $(r_q, g_q, b_q)$ where $r_q = r \gg 2$ etc.: $$\text{echo}(r_q, g_q, b_q) = \arg\min_{e \in [0,100]} \sqrt{(R_e - r)^2 + (G_e - g)^2 + (B_e - b)^2}$$
  3. Convert each pixel: $\text{gray} = \text{echo} \times 2.55$, yielding 0–255 grayscale.

1.2 Rotation & Surface Alignment

  1. Rotate 90° clockwise — original image has depth along horizontal; rotate so depth = vertical (row 0 = shallowest).
  2. Per-column surface detection: For each column $c$, find smallest row $r$ where $\text{gray}(r, c) \geq 15$. Call this surfaceRow[c].
  3. Gaussian smooth the surface profile with $\sigma = 3.0$ pixels (prevents single-pixel noise).
  4. Shift each column upward by surfaceRow[c] so skin surface = row 0.
  5. Crop to 3.0mm depth: keep only the first $\lfloor 3.0 \times \text{pxPerMm} \rfloor$ rows.

$$\text{pxPerMm} = \frac{\text{imageHeight (after rotation)}}{\text{totalDepthMm}} \quad \text{where totalDepthMm} = 20.0$$

2. Layer Segmentation

2.1 Epidermis Detection (Valley Method)

  1. Compute mean A-line: $\bar{I}(z) = \frac{1}{W} \sum_{c=0}^{W-1} \text{gray}(z, c)$ for each row $z$.
  2. Search first 0.5mm ($\lfloor 0.5 \times \text{pxPerMm} \rfloor$ rows) for peak: $z_{\text{peak}} = \arg\max_z \bar{I}(z)$.
  3. Set epiStartPx: scan backward from peak, find first row where $\bar{I}(z) \geq 0.40 \times \bar{I}(z_{\text{peak}})$.
  4. DEJ detection: scan forward from peak, stop at first row satisfying any:
    • Valley: $\bar{I}(z) < \bar{I}(z-1)$ and $\bar{I}(z) < \bar{I}(z+1)$ (local minimum)
    • 30% drop: $\bar{I}(z) < 0.30 \times \bar{I}(z_{\text{peak}})$
    • Rising again: $\bar{I}(z) > \bar{I}(z-1) + 2$
  5. Cap: If $(z_{\text{DEJ}} - z_{\text{epiStart}}) / \text{pxPerMm} > 0.30\,\text{mm}$, clamp DEJ to $z_{\text{epiStart}} + \lfloor 0.30 \times \text{pxPerMm} \rfloor$.

2.2 Adaptive 3-Tier Dermal Segmentation (Per-Column)

All boundaries follow skin surface undulation — computed per column $c$.

Papillary Dermis Bottom:

$$T_{\text{pap}} = \min(1.5 \times T_{\text{epi}},\; 0.18\,\text{mm})$$ $$z_{\text{papBottom}}[c] = z_{\text{DEJ}}[c] + \lfloor T_{\text{pap}} \times \text{pxPerMm} \rfloor$$

Hypodermis Detection (per-column):

  1. Compute plateau mean: average gray of column $c$ from $z_{\text{DEJ}} + 0.3\text{mm}$ to $z_{\text{DEJ}} + 1.0\text{mm}$. (Avoids entry echo bleed.)
  2. Set drop threshold: $\text{thresh} = \max(0.30 \times \text{plateauMean},\; 15)$.
  3. Scan downward from $z_{\text{DEJ}} + 0.5\text{mm}$. Mark "dark" if column gray $< \text{thresh}$.
  4. Find sustained run: $\geq \max(5, \lfloor 0.25\text{mm} \times \text{pxPerMm} \rfloor)$ consecutive dark pixels.
  5. $z_{\text{hypo}}[c] = $ start of sustained run. Clamp: $z_{\text{hypo}} \leq z_{\text{DEJ}} + 2.8\text{mm}$.

Reticular Dermis Split:

$$z_{\text{retMid}}[c] = z_{\text{papBottom}}[c] + \left\lfloor \frac{z_{\text{hypo}}[c] - z_{\text{papBottom}}[c]}{2} \right\rfloor$$
TierNameTopBottom
1Papillary (유두진피)$z_{\text{DEJ}}$$z_{\text{papBottom}}$
2Sup. Reticular (상부 망상)$z_{\text{papBottom}}$$z_{\text{retMid}}$
3Deep Reticular (하부 망상)$z_{\text{retMid}}$$z_{\text{hypo}}$

3. Acoustic Shadow Detection

Per-column detection of probe contact failure or acoustic dropout:

  1. For each column $c$, count pixels in $[z_{\text{DEJ}}, z_{\text{hypo}})$ where $\text{gray} < 10$.
  2. Compute $\text{darkRatio}[c] = \text{darkCount} / (z_{\text{hypo}} - z_{\text{DEJ}})$.
  3. If $\text{darkRatio} \geq 0.60$: column is shadowed → validColumn[c] = false.
Exclusion scope: Shadowed columns are excluded from ALL downstream computations: densitometry (LEP/MEP/HEP counts), GLCM texture, RVI, TCD, Delta gradients, Hexa-Core patch extraction, and thickness averaging.

4. Pixel Densitometry (LEP / MEP / HEP)

4.1 Rayleigh-Compensated LEP Threshold

$$\text{LEP}_{\max}(f) = \text{round}\!\left(30 \times \left(\frac{50}{f}\right)^{0.35}\right)$$

ClassGray range (10MHz)Acoustic meaningDermascan color
LEP0 – 53Fluid, micro-edema, voidsBlack → Green

4.3 Per-Column Counting

For each tier, loop over valid columns only, classifying each pixel within $[z_{\text{top}}[c], z_{\text{bottom}}[c])$:

for each col c where validColumn[c] == true:
  for each row z in [zTop[c], zBottom[c]):
    gray = image[z * width + c]
    if gray <= LEP_MAX: lepCount++
    else if gray <= 120: mepCount++
    else: hepCount++

5. Hexa-Core Biomechanical Engine — Full Specification

Reproducibility Note: All 6 indices are computed independently per anatomical tier (Papillary, Sup. Reticular, Deep Reticular) using the adaptive per-column boundaries from Section 2. All shadowed columns are excluded.

5.0 Tier ROI Patch Extraction (Shared Preprocessing)

FFT requires a rectangular patch. Extract from irregular per-column boundaries:

  1. Collect boundaries from valid columns only: validTops[], validBots[], validCols[].
  2. Compute median of valid tops → medTop; median of valid bots → medBot.
  3. R = max(2, medBot − medTop) (rows), C = len(validCols) (columns).
  4. Build patch $P[r][c]$: for $r \in [0, R)$, $c \in [0, C)$: $$P[r][c] = \text{aligned}[(\text{medTop} + r) \times W + \text{validCols}[c]]$$
If fewer than 4 valid columns exist, fall back to using ALL columns.

5.1 Shared FFT Computation (Used by BCT and CAI)

Both BCT and CAI share the same 2D FFT power spectrum. Compute once per tier:

  1. 2D Hanning window: $w[i][j] = \frac{1}{2}(1 - \cos\frac{2\pi i}{R-1}) \times \frac{1}{2}(1 - \cos\frac{2\pi j}{C-1})$
  2. Apply window: $P_w[i][j] = P[i][j] \times w[i][j]$
  3. Zero-pad to next power of 2: $R' = 2^{\lceil \log_2 R \rceil}$, $C' = 2^{\lceil \log_2 C \rceil}$
  4. Row-wise 1D FFT (Cooley-Tukey radix-2) on each of $R'$ rows
  5. Column-wise 1D FFT on each of $C'$ columns
  6. Compute power: $|F[i][j]|^2 = \text{Re}^2 + \text{Im}^2$
  7. DC-center shift: swap quadrants so DC is at $(R'/2, C'/2)$: $$\text{power}[(i + R'/2) \bmod R'][(j + C'/2) \bmod C'] = |F[i][j]|^2$$

Resulting powerSpectrum[R'][C'] has DC at center, usable for both BCT and CAI.

5.2 ① BCT — Bundle Caliber Thickness

Goal: Ratio of low-frequency (large structures, ≥50μm) to high-frequency (fine structures, <50μm) power.

Parameters:

ParameterValueMeaning
BUNDLE_CUTOFF50 μmCollagen bundle diameter threshold
$r_{\text{bundle}}$$1 / (50 \times 10^{-3}\text{mm}) = 20$ cycles/mmSpatial frequency cutoff
$\varepsilon$$10^{-10}$Division-by-zero guard

Algorithm:

  1. Set center: $r_h = R'/2$, $c_h = C'/2$.
  2. Convert cutoff to pixel frequency: $$r_{\text{cutoff}} = r_{\text{bundle}} \times \frac{\min(R', C')}{2 \times \text{pxPerMm}}$$
  3. Set max radius: $r_{\max} = \min(r_h, c_h)$.
  4. For each pixel $(i, j)$ in the power spectrum: 
    di = i - rHalf
dj = j - cHalf
r = sqrt(di² + dj²)
if r < 1 or r > rMax: skip  // exclude DC and beyond Nyquist
p = powerSpectrum[i][j]
if r <= rCutoff: lowPower += p
else:            highPower += p
  5. $$\boxed{\text{BCT} = \frac{P_{\text{low}}}{P_{\text{high}} + \varepsilon}}$$
Interpretation: BCT > 1.5 → thick, mature Type I bundles. BCT < 0.5 → fragmented, fine fibrils dominant (photoaging).

5.3 ② TCM — Total Collagen Mass

Goal: Combine bundle caliber with collagen pixel density for total mass estimate.

Parameters:

SymbolValueSource
$W_{\text{MEP}}$0.4MEP partial bundle weight (Type III fibrils 10–50μm)
$k_{\text{norm}}$100Normalization scale

Algorithm:

  1. From densitometry of this tier, obtain $N_{\text{HEP}}$, $N_{\text{MEP}}$, $N_{\text{total}}$.
  2. Compute effective bundle fraction: $$\phi_{\text{bundle,eff}} = \frac{N_{\text{HEP}} + 0.4 \times N_{\text{MEP}}}{N_{\text{total}}}$$
  3. $$\boxed{\text{TCM} = \min\!\Big(100,\; \max\!\big(0,\; \text{BCT}^2 \times \phi_{\text{bundle,eff}} \times 100\big)\Big)}$$
Range: 0–100. Higher = denser, thicker collagen matrix.

5.4 ③ PAI — Parallel Alignment Index

Goal: Measure fiber alignment anisotropy using the structure tensor.

Parameters:

SymbolValueMeaning
$\varepsilon$$10^{-10}$Division guard

Algorithm:

  1. Compute image gradients using central differences on the tier patch $P[R][C]$: 
    for r = 1 to R-2:
  for c = 1 to C-2:
    Ix[r][c] = (P[r][c+1] - P[r][c-1]) / 2    // horizontal gradient
    Iz[r][c] = (P[r+1][c] - P[r-1][c]) / 2    // vertical (depth) gradient
  2. Accumulate global structure tensor (uniform weighting): 
    Jxx = Σ Ix[r][c]²  / N
Jxz = Σ Ix[r][c] * Iz[r][c] / N
Jzz = Σ Iz[r][c]²  / N
    where $N$ = number of interior pixels $(R-2) \times (C-2)$.
  3. Solve 2×2 eigenvalue problem: $$\text{trace} = J_{xx} + J_{zz}, \quad \det = J_{xx} J_{zz} - J_{xz}^2$$ $$\text{disc} = \sqrt{\max(0,\; \text{trace}^2/4 - \det)}$$ $$\lambda_1 = \text{trace}/2 + \text{disc}, \quad \lambda_2 = \text{trace}/2 - \text{disc}$$
  4. Compute anisotropy: $$\boxed{\text{PAI} = \left(\frac{\lambda_1 - \lambda_2}{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \varepsilon}\right)^2}$$
Range: 0 (perfectly isotropic, disordered) → 1 (perfectly aligned parallel fibers).

5.5 ④ CAI — Collagen Alignment Index

Goal: Ratio of horizontal vs vertical spectral energy, indicating gravity-resistance capacity.

Parameters:

SymbolValueMeaning
Wedge half-angle15°Angular width of each wedge
$\varepsilon$$10^{-10}$Division guard

Algorithm (uses same FFT power spectrum as BCT):

  1. For each pixel $(i, j)$ in the DC-centered power spectrum: 
    di = i - R'/2
dj = j - C'/2
r = sqrt(di² + dj²)
if r < 1 or r > min(R'/2, C'/2): skip

// angle from horizontal (atan2 uses vertical=di, horizontal=dj)
angle = |atan2(di, dj)|     // range [0, π]

// Horizontal wedge: angle ≈ 0° or ≈ 180°
if angle < 15° * π/180  OR  angle > π - 15° * π/180:
    E_H += power[i][j] × r   // weight by radius for scale invariance

// Vertical wedge: angle ≈ 90°
if |angle - π/2| < 15° * π/180:
    E_V += power[i][j] × r
  2. $$\boxed{\text{CAI} = \frac{E_H - E_V}{E_H + E_V + \varepsilon}}$$
Range: −1 (pure vertical structures) → 0 (isotropic) → +1 (pure horizontal laminar structure). Positive = anti-gravity tension lines intact.

5.6 ⑤ LTI — Lateral Tension Integrity

Goal: Measure continuity of horizontal collagen cables via run-length statistics.

Parameters:

SymbolValueMeaning
Gray threshold120MEP/HEP boundary (structural pixel = gray > 120)
Closing kernel1 × 5 (horizontal)Bridge small gaps up to 2px

Algorithm:

  1. Binary mask: $M[r][c] = 1$ if $P[r][c] > 120$, else $0$.
  2. Horizontal morphological closing (dilation then erosion with 1×5 kernel): 
    halfK = 2
// Dilation: D[r][c] = max(M[r][c-2..c+2])
for each r, c:
    D[r][c] = OR of M[r][max(0,c-2)..min(C-1,c+2)]

// Erosion: E[r][c] = min(D[r][c-2..c+2])
for each r, c:
    E[r][c] = AND of D[r][max(0,c-2)..min(C-1,c+2)]
  3. Run-length extraction per row: 
    sumL2 = 0, sumL = 0
for each row r:
    runLen = 0
    for c = 0 to C-1:
        if E[r][c] == 1:
            runLen++
        else:
            if runLen > 0:
                sumL2 += runLen²
                sumL  += runLen
            runLen = 0
    // flush last run
    if runLen > 0:
        sumL2 += runLen²
        sumL  += runLen
  4. $$\boxed{\text{LTI} = \frac{\sum L_i^2}{C \times \sum L_i}}$$ where $C$ = number of columns in the patch.
    If $\sum L_i = 0$: LTI = 0.
Interpretation: The $L^2$ weighting means a single run of length 10 contributes 100, while 10 runs of length 1 contribute only 10. This specifically rewards long continuous collagen cables and penalizes fragmentation.

Range: 0 (completely fragmented) → 1 (single continuous horizontal fiber spanning full width).

5.7 ⑥ FWL — Free-Water Leakage

Goal: Estimate interstitial free water accumulation from structural integrity metrics. Not a direct measurement — derived from the Structure-Hydration Decoupling axiom.

Parameters:

SymbolValueSource
$W_{\text{base}}$40%Raman spectroscopy baseline (physiological minimum)
$\Delta W_{\max}$18%Maximum additional leakage above baseline
Exponential decay1.2BCT damping coefficient
Clamp range[40%, 58%]Physiological bounds

Formula:

$$\boxed{\text{FWL} = \text{clamp}\!\bigg(40 + 18 \times \left[1 - \frac{\text{PAI} + \text{LTI}}{2}\right] \times e^{-1.2 \times \text{BCT}},\;\; 40,\;\; 58\bigg)}$$

Derivation logic:

  • When PAI + LTI → 0 (no structural integrity): leak term = $18 \times e^{-1.2 \cdot \text{BCT}}$
  • When PAI + LTI → 2 (perfect structure): leak term = 0 → FWL = 40% (baseline)
  • When BCT → 0 (no bundle mass): $e^0 = 1$ → maximum leakage
  • When BCT → ∞ (thick bundles): $e^{-\infty} = 0$ → baseline even without alignment

6. Health Score

Composite 0–100 score aggregating all 6 Hexa-Core indices across 3 tiers:

$$\boxed{\text{HS} = \sum_{t=1}^{3} w_t \times S_t}$$
TierWeight $w_t$Rationale
Papillary0.35PVR-sensitive, hydration reservoir
Sup. Reticular0.40Primary structural zone, most clinical relevance
Deep Reticular0.25Energy device target zone

Per-tier sub-score $S_t$:

$$S_t = \Big(0.30 \cdot \hat{T} + 0.25 \cdot \text{PAI} + 0.20 \cdot \text{LTI} + 0.10 \cdot \hat{C} + 0.15 \cdot (1 - \hat{F})\Big) \times 100$$

Normalization transforms:

RawNormalizedLogic
TCM ∈ [0,100]$\hat{T} = \min(1, \text{TCM}/80)$80+ is perfect
CAI ∈ [−1,1]$\hat{C} = \max(0, (\text{CAI}+0.3)/0.8)$−0.3 → 0, +0.5 → 1
FWL ∈ [40,58]$\hat{F} = \max(0, (\text{FWL}-40)/18)$40% → 0 (good), 58% → 1 (bad)

7. Legacy Metrics

7.1 PVR — Papillary Void Ratio

$$\text{PVR} = \frac{N_{\text{LEP,pap}}}{N_{\text{MEP,pap}} + N_{\text{HEP,pap}}}$$

7.2 RVI — Reticular Void Index

$$\text{RVI} = \frac{\text{LEP\%}_{\text{ret}}}{100} \times \left(1 - \frac{\bar{I}_{\text{ret}}}{120}\right) \times 100$$

7.3 RSS — Reticular Solid Stiffness

$$\text{RSS} = \frac{N_{\text{HEP}}}{N_{\text{total}}} \times \left(1 - \frac{N_{\text{LEP}}}{N_{\text{total}}}\right) \times 100$$

7.4 Layer Deficit Gradients

$$\Delta_{\text{pap}} = \frac{\text{LEP\%}_{\text{pap}}}{\max(\text{LEP\%}_{\text{deep}},\; 1.0)}, \qquad \Delta_{\text{ret}} = \frac{\text{LEP\%}_{\text{ret}}}{\max(\text{LEP\%}_{\text{deep}},\; 1.0)}$$

7.5 GLCM Texture

$N_g = 128$ (gray quantized by $\gg 1$). Minimum ROI height: 15 rows (auto-expand if needed).
